name: Timothy Geithner

summary.text: Timothy F. Geithner was the ninth president and chief executive of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from November 17, 2003 until January 2009, serving as vice chairman of the Federal Open Market Committee, and was the 75th Secretary of the Treasury from January 26, 2009 to January 25, 2013. He joined the Treasury in 1988, served as Under Secretary for International Affairs under Robert Rubin and Lawrence Summers, and directed the IMF's Policy Development and Review Department from 2001 to 2003. As New York Fed president during the 2008 crisis he worked closely with Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke and Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson; SIGTARP later examined his role in the decision to pay AIG's swap counterparties effectively at par.

facts.claim: Geithner became the ninth president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on November 17, 2003, a role in which he served as vice chairman and a permanent member of the Federal Open Market Committee.
facts.quote: He became the ninth president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on November 17, 2003. In that capacity, he served as the vice chairman and a permanent member of the Federal Open Market Committee

facts.claim: Geithner served as the 75th Secretary of the Treasury from January 26, 2009 to January 25, 2013, and was the first former member of Treasury's career civil service to become Secretary.
facts.quote: Timothy F. Geithner served as the 75th Secretary of the Treasury from January 26, 2009 to January 25, 2013.

facts.claim: Before the New York Fed, Geithner joined the Treasury in 1988, served as Under Secretary for International Affairs under Secretaries Rubin and Summers, and from 2001 to 2003 directed the Policy Development and Review Department at the International Monetary Fund.
facts.quote: From 2001-2003, he was director of the Policy Development and Review Department at the International Monetary Fund.

sources.title: Timothy F. Geithner

facts.claim: Federal Reserve History states that as New York Fed president Geithner was directly involved in many pivotal policymaking decisions during the financial crisis that started in 2007, working closely with Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke and Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson.
facts.quote: As president of the New York Fed, Geithner was directly involved in many pivotal policymaking decisions made during the financial crisis that started in 2007. He worked closely with the chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Ben Bernanke, and the secretary of the Treasury, Henry Paulson.

facts.claim: SIGTARP reported in November 2009 that Geithner and the New York Fed's general counsel told it the financial condition of AIG's counterparties was not a relevant factor in the decision to create Maiden Lane III and pay the counterparties effectively at par.
facts.quote: Geithner and the BRBNY General Counsel told SIGTARP that the financial condition of the counterparties was not a relevant factor in the decision to create Maiden Lane III and pay counterparties effectively at par.

openQuestions: Site claim that Geithner 'oversaw the par-value Maiden Lane III payouts': supported in substance by SIGTARP-10-003, which examined the New York Fed's decision during his presidency and quotes his account of it.
Federal Reserve History lists Geithner's New York Fed tenure as 2003-2008 while Treasury gives 2003-2009; the Treasury date (he took office on January 26, 2009) appears to be the resignation date.
The site's Maiden Lane entry lists Geithner alongside Larry Fink and Hank Paulson as 'insiders'; no source returned describes any direct Geithner-BlackRock dealing.
